Title: Verify that a shop owner can create an order for their own shop using JWT authentication
Preconditions: 1. A shop owner is authenticated and has a valid JWT token. 2. The shop owner has a shop with ID 1. 3. At least one item exists in the shop.

Title: Verify that a shop owner cannot create an order for a shop they do not own
Preconditions: 1. A shop owner is authenticated and has a valid JWT token. 2. The shop owner does not own shop with ID 2.

Title: Verify that a shop owner can retrieve workers only from their own shop using JWT authentication
Preconditions: 1. A shop owner is authenticated and has a valid JWT token. 2. The shop owner owns shop with ID 1. 3. Shop with ID 1 has at least one worker.
Steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/shops/1/workers?page=0&limit=10 using the JWT token of the shop owner. 2. Verify the response status and body.

Title: Verify that an expired JWT token returns an appropriate error response
Preconditions: 1. A user has an expired JWT token. 2. The user attempts to access a protected endpoint.
Steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/shops/1/workers with the expired JWT token in the Authorization header. 2. Verify the response status and body.

Title: Verify that an invalid JWT token returns an appropriate error response
Preconditions: 1. A user has an invalid JWT token. 2. The user attempts to access a protected endpoint.
Steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/shops/1/workers with an invalid JWT token in the Authorization header. 2. Verify the response status and body.

Title: Verify successful authentication with valid JWT token for protected API endpoints
Preconditions: A valid JWT token is available for a registered user (shop owner)
Expected Result:
1. HTTP 200 OK response with status 'success' and a paginated list of workers in the 'data' field.
2. HTTP 201 Created response with status 'success', message 'Order created successfully', and the created order details including 'orderId' in the 'data' field.

Title: Verify authentication failure with expired JWT token
Preconditions: An expired JWT token is available for a registered user
Steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/shops/{shopId}/workers with the Authorization header containing 'Bearer <expired-jwt-token>'. Use any shopId.
Expected Result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized response with a JSON body containing: {"status": 401, "error": "Unauthorized", "code": "TOKEN_EXPIRED", "message": "Your session has expired. Please login again."}

Title: Verify authentication failure with invalid JWT token
Preconditions: An invalid JWT token is available (e.g., malformed or tampered token)
Steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/shops/{shopId}/workers with the Authorization header containing 'Bearer <invalid-jwt-token>'. Use any shopId.
Expected Result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized response with a JSON body containing: {"status": 401, "error": "Unauthorized", "code": "TOKEN_INVALID", "message": "Invalid token. Please login again."}

Title: Verify shop owner can access and modify orders for their own shop only
Preconditions: A valid JWT token is available for a shop owner who owns shop with ID 1 but not shop with ID 2

Title: Verify shop owner can add a new worker and set their PIN after OTP verification
Preconditions: A valid JWT token is available for a shop owner who owns shop with ID 1. A worker email is available for OTP delivery.
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/shops/1/workers/send-otp with the payload in testData.
2. Retrieve the OTP sent to the worker's email.
3. Send a POST request to /api/shops/1/workers/set-pin with the payload in testData, including the OTP from step 2.

Test Data: Step 1: {
  "name": "New Worker",
  "phone": "+15551234567",
  "email": "worker@example.com",
  "address": "123 Worker St"
}

Step 3: {
  "phoneNumber": "+15551234567",
  "otp": "123456",
  "pin": "1234",
  "confirmPin": "1234"
}
Expected Result:
1. HTTP 200 OK response with status 'success' and message 'OTP sent to your email'.
2. OTP is received at the worker's email address.
3. HTTP 200 OK response with status 'success' and message 'Worker PIN set successfully'. The worker can now authenticate using their phone number and PIN.

Title: Verify the new feature flag 'app.security.config2.enabled' is respected and does not break existing functionality when disabled
Preconditions: 1. Application is deployed with the updated application.properties. 2. No other changes to security-related configurations.
Steps:
1. Start the application. 2. Perform a security-sensitive operation (e.g., login, token generation). 3. Observe application logs and behavior.

Test Data: app.security.config2.enabled=false (new setting)
Expected Result: 1. Application starts without errors. 2. Security-sensitive operations complete successfully without errors or unexpected behavior. 3. No errors or warnings related to 'app.security.config2.enabled' appear in logs.

Title: Verify the application behaves correctly when the new feature flag 'app.security.config2.enabled' is absent or commented out
Preconditions: 1. Application is deployed with the new feature flag removed or commented out from application.properties. 2. No other changes to security-related configurations.
Steps:
1. Start the application. 2. Perform a security-sensitive operation (e.g., login, token generation). 3. Observe application logs and behavior.

Test Data: app.security.config2.enabled (absent or commented out)
Expected Result: 1. Application starts without errors. 2. Security-sensitive operations complete successfully without errors or unexpected behavior. 3. No errors or warnings related to missing 'app.security.config2.enabled' appear in logs.

Title: Verify the project builds successfully with the updated pom.xml and produces the correct artifact
Preconditions: 1. Clean the project (e.g., mvn clean). 2. Ensure no local or remote dependency conflicts exist.
Steps:
1. Run the build command (e.g., mvn clean install). 2. Observe the build output and logs. 3. Check the target directory for the generated artifact.

Test Data: pom.xml (no version changes, only formatting)
Expected Result: 1. Build completes with SUCCESS status. 2. Artifact is generated in the target directory with the correct name (TailorBookApp-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar). 3. No dependency resolution errors or warnings appear in logs.
